title: Register-copying loop
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state multitape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, and let $s$ be a copy-loop mode. Given eleven-register values $\rho$ with scratch register value zero, and an input position $p$, the program reaches the exit mode with the destination register increased by the initial source-register value, all other register values unchanged, and input position still $p$. For every output prefix, this occurs within $7a+2$ steps, where $a$ is the initial value of the source register, and the program leaves the output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state multitape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
the scratch register has value zero: $\rho(\mathrm{TMP})=0$
